angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 551,968 km at 108.47 pc = 0.07 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 9.2187 +/- 0.0134 mas (same row, RUWE 0.87): 108.47 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.7934 +/- 0.0465 solar radii from Mistry et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-4308 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166....9M/abstract): 551,968 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.9 +/- 0.1133 solar masses from Mistry et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-4308 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166....9M/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5243 +/- 126 K from Mistry et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-4308 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166....9M/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Mistry et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-4308 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166....9M/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-4308.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.593, rounded to two decimals
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-4308 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.36795, from TICv8 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2019AJ....158..138S/abstract)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
